subject: woolly sheep
title: What If a Sheep Was Never Sheared? One Hid in Caves for Six Years

scenes.text: What if a sheep was never sheared? The wool never stops, and that's the danger.
Wild sheep shed their coats. Wool breeds have had that bred out, so the fleece just keeps growing.
New Zealand's Shrek dodged the shearers for six years by hiding in caves. Caught in 2004, he carried 27 kilos of wool. A normal fleece is about four and a half.
In 2015, walkers near Canberra found Chris: at least five years unshorn, barely able to get up and walk.
Carers gave him weeks to live. Urine trapped in the fleece had burned his skin.
A champion shearer took about 45 minutes. The fleece weighed just over 40 kilos, a world record. Chris walked away at half his weight.

description:
What if a sheep was never sheared? Its wool would simply keep growing.
Domestic sheep raised for wool have been bred not to shed their fleece. Shrek, a New Zealand merino who avoided muster for six years by hiding in caves, carried 27 kilograms of wool when he was caught in 2004, about six times a normal fleece. Chris, found near Canberra in 2015 after at least five years unshorn, yielded just over 40 kilograms, recognised as the heaviest fleece on record; carers said he had only weeks to live.
